clue.text: A man with a seat in a cathedral — a throne with a jewel on it

definitions.text: A man with a seat in a cathedral

parts.note: slang for a lavatory, humorously called the throne, is a john
jasper is a semi-precious stone, so a jewel

explanation.surface: A churchman's seat in a cathedral is described as a jewelled throne.
explanation.walkthrough: JOHN JASPER is the choirmaster of Cloisterham Cathedral in Dickens's The Mystery of Edwin Drood, so he has a seat in a cathedral. 'Throne' is jokey slang for a lavatory, a john.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's choirmaster has his stall in Cloisterham Cathedral, a literal seat there.

clue.text: Nick and Jack having trouble

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards
to ail is to be unwell, to have trouble

explanation.surface: A man called Jack is caught out and in difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' is British slang for a prison, as in 'in the nick'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nick is British slang for a prison, as is the place where convicts are locked up.

clue.text: "I have ruined Doyce! The honest, self -, indefatigable old man" (Little Dorrit)

definitions.text: "I have ruined Doyce! The honest, self -, indefatigable old man" (Little Dorrit)

parts.words: "I have ruined Doyce! The honest, self -, indefatigable old man" (Little Dorrit)
parts.note: a quotation from Dickens's Little Dorrit with a word missing after 'self-', which the solver supplies to complete the compound

explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Clennam laments ruining his partner Daniel Doyce; Dickens calls Doyce 'the honest, self-helpful, indefatigable old man'.
explanation.definitionFit: The gap completes Dickens's compound describing Doyce as a man who relies on his own efforts.

clue.text: Beadle worked at London Transport, concealing drug — he was not to be trusted

definitions.text: he was not to be trusted

parts.note: Jeremy Beadle was a British television prankster, so Beadle gives his first name
did is a past tense of do, meaning worked or performed

indicators.note: the rail line's letters wrap around the drug, keeping it hidden inside

parts.note: the DLR, Docklands Light Railway, is part of London's transport network
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A TV prankster worked on the London Underground, hiding narcotics, and proved untrustworthy.
explanation.walkthrough: The DLR is the Docklands Light Railway. Jeremy Diddler is the sponging swindler of James Kenney's farce Raising the Wind, whose name gave English the verb 'diddle'.
explanation.definitionFit: The character is a stock swindler who borrows and never repays, a byword for an untrustworthy cheat.

clue.text: FBI agent's deceptive operation capturing a clever criminal finally

indicators.note: the operation's letters close round the next pieces, holding them like a captive

parts.note: a sting is a police operation that tricks criminals

indicators.note: applied to both words before it, it asks for the closing letter of each

explanation.surface: An FBI agent runs a sting that catches a cunning crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capturing' puts A plus R and L (the last letters of 'clever' and 'criminal') inside STING. Clarice STARLING is the FBI agent in Thomas Harris's The Silence of the Lambs.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarice is Thomas Harris's fictional federal investigator, the trainee who interviews Hannibal Lecter.

clue.text: Game in soup — a concoction needing crackers?

indicators.note: to be in the soup is to be in a mess, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Game meat floating in soup is a dish that needs crackers alongside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soup' signals a jumble of GAME and IN. The definition plays on crackers as biscuits served with soup and as people who crack codes or puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzle or code is something devised that has to be cracked by solvers.

clue.text: Some jazz singing is a form of punishment

parts.note: is shortened to 's gives S
the cat-o'-nine-tails was a whip used for flogging

explanation.surface: Wordless jazz vocals are presented as a kind of penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Ella Fitzgerald's improvised nonsense syllables sung in jazz are this style of vocalising.

clue.text: Agree with artist? That's not a realistic idea

parts.note: to chime in with something is to agree with it
RA is a Royal Academician, a conventional artist

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to go along with a painter's fanciful notion.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanciful notion is a wild fantasy, the sense taken from the mythical monster.

clue.text: Man possibly written about by Victoria Hislop

definitions.meaning: the Isle of Man is an example of a landmass surrounded by sea
Hislop's 2005 debut novel is set on Spinalonga, a former leper colony off Crete

explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person, but it is the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses name a landmass in the sea: Man is one, and Hislop's bestseller bears that title.

clue.text: In Italy, a Latin form of poetry mostly seen somewhere on the Adriatic coast

parts.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, its last letter dropped

parts.note: a lyric is a short poem expressing feeling

explanation.surface: In Italy, a type of Latin verse turns up somewhere along the Adriatic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the C from LYRIC. ILLYRIA was the ancient region on the eastern Adriatic, also the setting of Shakespeare's Twelfth Night.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient region lay along the Balkan shore of that sea, in modern Croatia and Albania.

clue.text: Legendary queen showing some intelligence in turbulent reign

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the jumbled letters
something turbulent is disturbed, so the letters are stirred up

parts.note: AI, artificial intelligence, is a kind of intelligence

explanation.surface: A queen of legend shows some brains during a troubled reign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turbulent' rearranges the letters of 'reign' to IGRNE. In Arthurian legend Igraine is King Arthur's mother, wife of Uther Pendragon.
explanation.definitionFit: In Arthurian legend she is Uther Pendragon's wife and Arthur's mother, hence a queen of myth.

clue.text: Sheena Mackay wrote this droll or choice novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A novelist is said to have written a witty or select book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the noun, but it is the adjective meaning new, signalling an anagram of DROLL OR CHOICE. Shena Mackay's Redhill Rococo won the Fawcett Prize in 1987.
explanation.definitionFit: Mackay's 1986 comic novel, set in the Surrey commuter town, is the book in question.

clue.text: A book reflecting wartime Europe and a household group of musicians

parts.note: a household is a family living together
Madness is a British ska and pop band

explanation.surface: A book about wartime Europe is paired with a domestic musical group.
explanation.walkthrough: MADNESS is a London ska band famous from the 1980s. Thomas Keneally's novel A Family Madness ties an Australian family to wartime Belarus.
explanation.definitionFit: Keneally's 1985 novel links modern Sydney to the Nazi occupation of Belarus, a story of the war years.

clue.text: Writer of tales of South London, with a local boy and sister as 24 might say

definitions.text: Writer of tales of South London

indicators.note: 24 across names the Oxford don famous for swapping initial sounds, so the sounds are exchanged

parts.note: Del Boy is the Peckham trader of the sitcom Only Fools and Horses, a South London lad
a nun is a religious sister

explanation.surface: A South London writer is described in local slang as a lad and a nun.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of DEL and NUN gives NELL DUNN by sound. Del Boy is the wheeler-dealer of the British sitcom Only Fools and Horses. Dunn wrote Up the Junction, set in Battersea.
explanation.definitionFit: Her stories of Battersea life, Up the Junction, made her the chronicler of that part of the capital.

clue.text: Scottish hooligan caused offence in uprising — he finally got a taste of his own medicine

definitions.text: he finally got a taste of his own medicine

parts.note: ned is Scottish slang for a young thug

indicators.note: in a down entry the word rises, so it is read from bottom to top

parts.note: sinned means did wrong, gave offence

explanation.surface: A Scottish thug who offended during a riot ends up suffering what he dealt out.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'uprising' reads the word from the bottom up. Ned Dennis is the hangman in Dickens's Barnaby Rudge, himself hanged after the Gordon Riots.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's executioner is himself sent to the gallows, suffering the fate he inflicted on others.

clue.text: One dwelling in a Mediterranean city, having a council home

indicators.note: one piece lives inside the city's letters

parts.note: Nice is a city on the French Riviera
a means one, as in 'a dozen'

explanation.surface: A resident of a Riviera city has a home owned by the local council.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dwelling in' puts A inside NICE to make NICAE. 'Council home' looks like British public housing, but it is the city that hosted the church councils of 325 and 787.
explanation.definitionFit: The city in Asia Minor hosted the first ecumenical gathering of bishops, which produced the Nicene Creed.

clue.text: John Fowles's log book?

parts.note: a title by the novelist that is also a term for part of a logarithm, the fractional digits after the point

explanation.definitionFit: Fowles's 1982 novel shares its title with the decimal part of a logarithm.

clue.text: Sailors originally dressed in flipping hat and skirt

indicators.note: the sailors and initial go inside the turned-round hat
flipping a hat turns it over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat
RN is the Royal Navy

indicators.note: taking the word at its origin, its opening letter

explanation.surface: Sailors first dressed in a hat turned upside down and a skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' turns the hat round to DIL. A lid is everyday slang for a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a full Alpine peasant skirt with a tight waistband, worn in Bavaria and Austria.

clue.text: Do something green? That's right — green twice over, almost

parts.note: green is given two ways: eco, as in environmentally friendly

indicators.note: almost the whole word is kept, its last letter dropped

parts.note: the second green is vert, the heraldic word for that colour

explanation.surface: Someone checks they are being eco-friendly, and is told yes, doubly so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the T from VERT, the heraldic name for green. The definition asks: is reclaiming and reusing material an environmentally friendly act?
explanation.definitionFit: To get back or reclaim waste material for reuse is a practice of recycling, an environmentally friendly act.

clue.text: A literary school or university payment method, according to 24

indicators.note: 24 across is the Oxford don whose name is given to swapped initial sounds, so the sounds are exchanged

parts.note: Yale is an American university
a card is a way to pay

explanation.surface: A school of writers is mistaken for a college or a way of paying.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of YALE and CARD gives KAILYARD. The Kailyard school was a group of sentimental Scottish writers, such as J M Barrie, in the 1890s.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names a movement of late-Victorian Scottish writers depicting cosy rural life.

clue.text: A planet nearer the sun? That's about right for somewhere hot

indicators.note: the planet's letters are placed around the next piece

parts.note: Venus orbits closer to the sun than Earth

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a planet is closer to the sun, which would explain the heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R inside VENUS. AVERNUS is the crater lake near Naples which the Romans took as the entrance to the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: The Romans believed the volcanic lake led down to the infernal regions, a place of fire.

clue.text: Frightful heel finally forgiven by a saintly character in a historical novel

definitions.text: saintly character in a historical novel

indicators.note: frightful means terrible, so the letters are mangled
it picks the closing letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A dreadful cad is ultimately pardoned by a holy figure in a period novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frightful' rearranges HEEL to HELE; 'finally' gives N from 'forgiven'. Evelyn Waugh's novel Helena tells of the mother of Constantine, who found the True Cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Waugh's 1950 novel portrays the Roman empress later canonised, a saint in fiction.

clue.text: Software provided to some people in a 1950s novel

parts.note: Excel is a Microsoft spreadsheet program
lent means provided on loan
women are some of the people

explanation.surface: A computer program is given to a group of people in a book from the fifties.
explanation.walkthrough: Barbara Pym's Excellent Women (1952) is a comedy of London spinsterhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbara Pym's 1952 comedy of manners is the book from that decade.

clue.text: A teacher leaving a South London area is an admirer of Merton

indicators.note: the teacher departs, so those letters come out of the place name

parts.note: Croydon is a borough in south London
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A teacher quits a South London suburb and turns out to be a fan of Merton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Merton' looks like the south London borough next to Croydon, but it is Merton Densher, loved by Kate CROY in Henry James's The Wings of the Dove.
explanation.definitionFit: In Henry James's novel Kate loves the journalist Densher, whose first name is given here.

clue.text: A raven's flying around King Ferdinand's home

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the royal abbreviation
flying suggests scattering, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the words as written, the 's adding no letter, give the letters to mix
R is for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A raven is flying round the palace of a king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' rearranges A RAVEN, and 'around' puts R inside it. In Love's Labour's Lost, Ferdinand is King of NAVARRE, a kingdom in the Pyrenees.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Love's Labour's Lost places its king's court in the Pyrenean kingdom.

clue.text: Victorian source of furious crazes, we hear?

definitions.text: Victorian source of furious crazes, we hear?

parts.words: Victorian source of furious crazes, we hear?
parts.note: said with swapped opening sounds, furious crazes becomes curious phrases, the kind of slip attributed to an Oxford don

explanation.definitionFit: The Oxford warden William Archibald was famed for transposing initial sounds, making odd phrases.

clue.text: A hint of red seen in blue gemstone

indicators.note: the hint is placed inside the word for blue

parts.note: blue means sad, down

indicators.note: a hint is a small amount, the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A trace of red shows up in a blue stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' puts R inside SAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Sard is a reddish-brown variety of chalcedony, cut as a semi-precious stone.

clue.text: Bathhouse producer from the east — very good one, embraced by a prime minister — heavens!

indicators.note: the reversed letters are hugged by the outer pieces

parts.note: Theresa May was a British prime minister
the sky is the heavens

indicators.note: in an across entry, reading from the east means right to left, so backwards

parts.note: OK means good, acceptable
a means one

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at a bathhouse builder, embraced by a premier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the east' turns V, OK and A into AKOV. Vladimir Mayakovsky wrote the satirical play The Bathhouse (1930); Theresa May was a British prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet poet wrote the satirical play of that name, so he produced it as author.
